newsitem.title: CHINA: China's scientists back laws to control cloning.
newsitem.headline: China's scientists back laws to control cloning.

text.p: China's scientists want laws enacted to control the risks presented by a recent breakthrough in clone technology, the official Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

Geneticist Zhang Jiaming said the creation of a carbon-copy sheep in Scotland -- the first time an adult animal has successfully been cloned -- was a leap equivalent to the discovery of nuclear fusion, presenting the same mix of risks and benefits to mankind.

The discovery, announced earlier this week, has sparked controversy around the world with scientists, politicians and editorial writers discussing the possibility that ways may be found to duplicate humans.

Zhang, a delegate to the annual meeting of China's parliament beginning on Saturday, said he and other scientists in the legislature agreed that laws should ban the cloning of human beings, Xinhua said.
"However, there is no need for panic since the technology has only made initial progress," Xinhua quoted the scientists as saying.

Chen Shouyi, head of the Institute of Genetics under the Chinese Academy of Sciences, told Xinhua the new technology could help maintain the quality of animal stock and should not be stopped "simply because of some potential dangers it may present".
